newsitem.title: UK: UK gilts settle lower on inflation, political woes.
newsitem.headline: UK gilts settle lower on inflation, political woes.

text.p: 1620 GMT - UK gilts pared afternoon losses late in the session, but still settled down on the day as political and inflation worries dogged the market. RPI figures disappointed and concerns over an early election allowed other markets to outperform. * March gilt futures settle at 113-10, down 6/32
The opposition Labour party will on Monday table a censure motion against Agriculture Minister Douglas Hogg, a move which could signal an imminent attempt to topple the government.

If the ruling Conservatives are defeated in Monday's vote, it would almost certainly prompt Labour to table a no-confidence motion in the government, probably for later in the week. If the government lost, an election could follow within weeks.
The March gilt future settled at 113-10, down 6/32.
"Added to the political worries were the inflation figures which were a big disappointment, certainly on a first reading," said the salesman.

UK underlying annual inflation rate was unchanged at 3.1 percent in January compared with the previous month, and remained subbornly above the government's 2.5 percent target. City forecasts centred on a small fall to 3.0 percent.
"The figures were not as bad as the first reading suggested. Big falls in the prices of clothing and footwear, and household goods was of some comfort," said a trader at GEMM.
He said while other markets outperformed gilts on Thursday, there was room for a reversal on Friday.
"There is scope for a recovery tomorrow. There has been good buying interest late in the day."
But the salesman said all international bond markets were a little wary of the auction later on Thursday of $10 billion of 30-year T-bonds, the last leg of the U.S. quarterly refunding.
"The other auctions have not been a great success. If the 30-year doesn't go well it will sour the European open tomorrow."
The spread between gilts and Bunds widened to 170 basis point compared with 164 on Wednesday.
Short sterling eased slightly. Both March and June slipped by 0.02 to settle at 93.70 and 93.47 respectively.
